title: Existence of Optimal Mixed Strategies (Loomis Foundations)
body_html:
Existence of Optimal Mixed Strategies (Loomis Foundations)

For a finite matrix game $A : I \times J \to \mathbb{R}$, the row player's guarantee function is $$\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}(x) = \min_{j \in J} \sum_{i \in I} x_i A(i,j),$$ and the column player's loss-cap function is $$\mu_{\mathrm{aux}}(y) = \max_{i \in I} \sum_{j \in J} y_j A(i,j).$$ The two scalar values $$\lambda_0 = \sup_{x \in \Delta(I)} \lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}(x) \quad \text{and} \quad \mu_0 = \inf_{y \in \Delta(J)} \mu_{\mathrm{aux}}(y)$$ are the maxmin and minmax values of the game.

This node packages four facts that hold before the inductive minimax identity is established:

  1. Continuity. Both $\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}$ and $\mu_{\mathrm{aux}}$ are continuous on the (compact) mixed-strategy simplices.
  2. Boundedness. $\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is bounded above and $\mu_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is bounded below by the obvious extremes of $A$.
  3. Achievement. There exist mixed strategies $x^\ast$ and $y^\ast$ such that $\sum_i x^\ast_i A(i,j) \ge \lambda_0$ for every column $j$ and $\sum_j y^\ast_j A(i,j) \le \mu_0$ for every row $i$.
  4. Weak duality. $\lambda_0 \le \mu_0$.
proof_html:
Continuity of $\lambda_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is the finite infimum of continuous weighted sums (Continuous.finset_inf'_apply); the proof for $\mu_{\mathrm{aux}}$ is dual. Boundedness follows because each weighted sum is bounded by the extreme matrix entry. The supremum $\lambda_0$ is achieved by the extreme-value theorem applied to the compact mixed-strategy simplex (IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn), and the optimiser realises $\lambda_0$ on every pure column by the infimum definition; the $\mu_0$ side is symmetric. Weak duality combines the two optimisers in the bilinear payoff: $$\lambda_0 \le \sum_{i,j} x^\ast_i y^\ast_j A(i,j) \le \mu_0,$$ using the pointwise-to-weighted bound transfer from Pointwise Bounds Are Simplex Bounds.

References

  • [MFoGT, Chapter 2, Section 2.3] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Existence of mixed optimisers and weak duality, prior to the inductive minimax theorem.

deps.title: Continuity on the Real Standard Simplex

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.lam.aux.continuous
lean_refs.signature:
theorem lam.aux.continuous (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    Continuous (lam.aux A)
lean_refs.docstring: `lam.aux A` is continuous as a function of the simplex point.

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.mu.aux.continuous
lean_refs.signature:
theorem mu.aux.continuous (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    Continuous (mu.aux A)
lean_refs.docstring: `mu.aux A` is continuous as a function of the simplex point.

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.lam.aux.bddAbove
lean_refs.signature:
theorem lam.aux.bddAbove (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    ∃ C, ∀ x, lam.aux A x ≤ C
lean_refs.docstring: `lam.aux A` is uniformly bounded above on the simplex.

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.mu.aux.bddBelow
lean_refs.signature:
theorem mu.aux.bddBelow (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    ∃ C, ∀ y, C ≤ mu.aux A y
lean_refs.docstring: `mu.aux A` is uniformly bounded below on the simplex.

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.lam.aux.le_lam0
lean_refs.signature:
theorem lam.aux.le_lam0 (A : I → J → ℝ) (x : stdSimplex ℝ I) :
    lam.aux A x ≤ lam0 A

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.mu.aux.ge_mu0
lean_refs.signature:
theorem mu.aux.ge_mu0 (A : I → J → ℝ) (y : stdSimplex ℝ J) :
    mu0 A ≤ mu.aux A y
lean_refs.docstring: The infimum `mu0` is dominated by every `mu.aux` value.

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.exists_xx_lam0
lean_refs.signature:
theorem exists_xx_lam0 (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    ∃ xx : stdSimplex ℝ I, ∀ j, lam0 A ≤ wsum xx (fun i => A i j)

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.exists_yy_mu0
lean_refs.signature:
theorem exists_yy_mu0 (A : I → J → ℝ) :
    ∃ yy : stdSimplex ℝ J, ∀ i, wsum yy (fun j => A i j) ≤ mu0 A

lean_refs.name: MinimaxLoomis.lam0_le_mu0
lean_refs.signature: theorem lam0_le_mu0 (A : I → J → ℝ) : lam0 A ≤ mu0 A
